children.translated_text: Vaidya 296
free from all faults, adorned with all virtues,
having bowed, I honor the Omniscient, the sole kinsman of all beings
O king, for the arising of <s>Dharma</s> (righteous conduct) for you, I will set forth the <s>Dharma</s> that is wholly salutary,

children.text: vakṣyāmi dharmaḥ siddhiṃ hi yāti saddharmabhājane // NRa_1.2 //
children.translated_text: I shall expound <s>Dharma</s>; for <s>sat-dharma</s> (true Dharma) attains success in one who is a worthy vessel
where first there is the rise of <s>abhyudaya</s> (worldly prosperity), and afterward the rise of <s>naiḥśreyasa</s> (the highest good),
for, having attained <s>abhyudaya</s>, one then proceeds in due order to <s>naiḥśreyasa</s>
therein, <s>abhyudaya</s> is happiness, and <s>naiḥśreyasa</s> is <s>mokṣa</s> (liberation),
the concise means for this are <s>śraddhā</s> (faith) and <s>prajñā</s> (wisdom)
by reason of <s>śraddhā</s>, one embraces <s>Dharma</s>; by reason of <s>prajñā</s>, one knows it in reality,

children.text: prajñā pradhānaṃ tvanayoḥ śraddhā pūrvaṃgamāsya tu // NRa_1.5 //
children.translated_text: of these two, <s>prajñā</s> is primary, yet <s>śraddhā</s> is its forerunner
who does not transgress <s>Dharma</s> out of desire, aversion, fear, or delusion,

children.text: sa śrāddha iti vijñeyaḥ śreyaso bhājanaṃ param // NRa_1.6 //
children.translated_text: that one is to be understood as faithful, the supreme vessel of the highest good
having thoroughly examined all action of body, speech, and mind,
knowing what benefits others and oneself, he should always do that; such a one is a wise man
Vaidya 297
non-harming, abstention from theft, avoidance of others’ wives,
restraint regarding falsehood, slander, harsh speech, and idle talk
avoidance of covetousness, ill will, and wrong view,

children.text: ete karmapathāḥ śuklā daśa kṛṣṇā viparyayāt // NRa_1.9 //
children.translated_text: these are the ten white <s>karmapathas</s> (paths of action); the black are their opposites
abstinence from intoxicants, right <s>ājīva</s> (livelihood), non-harming, giving with respect,

children.text: pūjyapūjā ca maitrī ca dharmaścaiṣa samāsataḥ // NRa_1.10 //
children.translated_text: honoring the honorable, and friendliness—this is <s>Dharma</s> in brief
from mere mortification of the body there is no <s>Dharma</s>; for by that,
there is neither abstention from harming others nor the benefiting of others
he who, disregarding the great highway of true <s>Dharma</s>—manifest as <s>dāna</s> (giving), <s>śīla</s> (moral conduct), and <s>kṣamā</s> (forbearance)—
goes by the wrong bypaths of bodily mortification,
enters the dreadful jungle of <s>saṃsāra</s> (the round of rebirth), with its trees of endless births,
his limbs swallowed by the serpents of the <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions), for a very long time
through harming, one is born short‑lived; through non‑harming, there are few illnesses,
through stealing, one becomes addicted to pleasures; through adultery, one is beset with enemies
from false speech, repudiation; from slander, the splitting of friends,
from roughness, the hearing of unpleasant things; from idle talk, speech that is ineffectual
covetous imagining destroys one’s hopes; ill will is said to bring fear,
wrong view results in being of wrong views; drinking intoxicants causes confusion of mind
by not giving, poverty; by wrong livelihood, deceit,
by arrogance, base birth; by envy, low vitality
from anger, an ugly complexion; from failing to question the wise, stupidity,

children.text: phalametanmanuṣyatve sarvebhyaḥ prāk ca durgatiḥ // NRa_1.18 //
children.translated_text: these are the fruits in human existence; prior to all of them, a bad destiny
such is the ripening (<s>vipāka</s>) of what is called the <s>akuśala</s> (unwholesome),

children.text: kuśalānāṃ ca sarveṣāṃ viparītaḥ phalodayaḥ // NRa_1.19 //
children.translated_text: for all the <s>kuśala</s> (wholesome), the opposite results arise

children.text: lobho dveṣaśca mohaśca tajjaṃ karmeti cāśubham /
children.translated_text: greed, hatred, and delusion—and the <s>karman</s> (action) born from them—are <s>aśubha</s> (unwholesome),
non‑greed, non‑delusion, and non‑hatred—and the <s>karman</s> (action) born from them—are <s>śubha</s> (wholesome)
from the <s>aśubha</s> (unwholesome) come all sufferings and all bad destinies,
from the <s>śubha</s> (wholesome) come all good destinies and happiness in every birth
cessation from all that is unwholesome, and constant engagement in the wholesome,

children.text: manasā karmaṇā vācā dharmo 'yaṃ dvividhaḥ smṛtaḥ // NRa_1.22 //
children.translated_text: this <s>Dharma</s> is remembered as twofold; [it is to be cultivated] by mind, by action, and by speech
by this <s>Dharma</s> one is freed from <s>naraka</s> (hells), <s>preta</s> (hungry-ghost), and <s>tiryak</s> (animal) realms,
and among humans and gods one attains happiness, splendor, and broad sovereignty
Vaidya 298
by means of <s>dhyāna</s> (meditative absorptions), the <s>apramāṇas</s> (the immeasurables), and the formless attainments (<s>arūpya</s>), one enjoys happiness up to <s>Brahmā</s>,
such is the <s>abhyudaya-dharma</s> (Dharma of worldly prosperity), and this is its fruit in brief
but the <s>naiḥśreyasa</s> <s>Dharma</s> (Dharma of the highest good) is subtle, with a profound vision,
declared by the <s>Jinas</s> (Victors) to terrify the childish and the hard of hearing

children.text: nāsmyahaṃ na bhaviṣyāmi na me 'sti na bhaviṣyati /
children.translated_text: “I am not; I will not be; nothing of mine exists; nothing of mine will exist”—

children.text: iti bālasya saṃtrāsaḥ paṇḍitasya bhayakṣayaḥ // NRa_1.26 //
children.translated_text: such is the terror of the childish; for the wise, it is the cessation of fear
this is born of <s>ahaṃkāra</s> (ego-conceit), accompanied by <s>mamakāra</s> (the notion of “mine”),
All beings have been addressed by the one who speaks solely for the welfare of beings,
“‘I exist,’ and ‘what is mine exists as well’—this is false for those who seek the ultimate truth,
for, through knowledge of things as they really are, neither of the two obtains
the <s>skandhas</s> (aggregates) arise from <s>ahaṃkāra</s> (ego‑conceit), yet that <s>ahaṃkāra</s> is unreal in fact;

children.text: bījaṃ yasyānṛtaṃ tasya prarohaḥ satyataḥ kutaḥ // NRa_1.29 //
children.translated_text: when the seed is unreal, how could its sprout be real
thus, seeing the <s>skandhas</s> to be not real, <s>ahaṃkāra</s> is abandoned;
and with the abandonment of <s>ahaṃkāra</s>, there is no further arising of the <s>skandhas</s>
just as, taking up a mirror, one apprehends the reflection of one’s own face;

children.text: dṛśya) te nāma taccaivaṃ na kiṃcidapi tattvataḥ // NRa_1.31 //
children.translated_text: that is seen indeed, yet in reality there is nothing there
so too, <s>ahaṃkāra</s> is apprehended by taking up the <s>skandhas</s>,

children.text: na ca kaścitsa tattvena svamukhapratibimbavat // NRa_1.32 //
children.translated_text: and yet, in truth, there is no such entity—just like the reflection of one’s face
and just as, without taking up a mirror, the reflection of one’s own face is not seen,
so, without taking up the <s>skandhas</s>, the notion ‘I’ is not [seen] either
hearing such teachings, <s>Āryānanda</s>, having obtained the <s>dharmacakṣus</s> (Dharma‑eye),
himself repeatedly instructed the monks
so long as there is grasping at the <s>skandhas</s>, so long there is also the notion ‘I’,

children.text: ahaṃkāre sati punaḥ karma janma tataḥ punaḥ // NRa_1.35 //
children.translated_text: and when <s>ahaṃkāra</s> is present, then again there is <s>karma</s> (action), and from that, again, <s>janma</s> (birth)
this triple‑tracked circle of <s>saṃsāra</s> (round of rebirth), without beginning, middle, or end,
whirls like a circle of a firebrand, being mutually conditioned
because it is not apprehended as self, as other, or as both, nor in any of the three times (past, present, future),

children.text: ahaṃkāraḥ kṣayaṃ yāti tataḥ karma ca janma ca // NRa_1.37 //
children.translated_text: <s>ahaṃkāra</s> comes to cessation—and thereby <s>karma</s> and birth as well
thus, seeing the arising of cause and effect, and also their cessation,

children.text: nāstitāmastitāṃ caiva naiti lokasya tattvataḥ // NRa_1.38 //
children.translated_text: one does not, in truth, adopt the extremes of ‘non‑existence’ or ‘existence’ regarding the world
Vaidya 299
hearing thus of the cessation of all suffering—which is <s>Dharma</s>—the unexamining person trembles,
from not understanding, fearful even of the fearless state

children.text: na bhaviṣyati nirvāṇe sarvametanna te bhayam /
children.translated_text: ‘In <s>nirvāṇa</s> (quiescence) all this will not exist’—let there be no fear for you;

children.text: ucyamāna ihābhāvastasya te kiṃ bhayaṃkaraḥ // NRa_1.40 //
children.translated_text: it is the non‑existence here and now, in his case, that is being spoken of—why should that frighten you

children.text: mokṣe nātmā na ca skandhā mokṣaścedīdṛśaḥ priyaḥ /
children.translated_text: in <s>mokṣa</s> (liberation) there is no <s>ātman</s> (self) nor are there <s>skandhas</s>; if such liberation is dear to you,
why is the removal of the self and the <s>skandhas</s> even here displeasing to you

children.text: na cābhāvo 'pi nirvānaṃ kuta eva tasya[vāsya] bhāvatā /
children.translated_text: nor is <s>nirvāṇa</s> mere non‑being—how could it possess being,
<s>nirvāṇa</s> is said to be the cessation of the preoccupation with being and non‑being
in brief, the <s>nāstitā‑dṛṣṭi</s> (view of non‑existence)—‘there is no fruit of action’—
is unwholesome, leading to bad destinies; this is remembered as wrong view
in brief, the <s>astitā‑dṛṣṭi</s> (view of existence)—‘there is fruit of actions’—
is meritorious, tending toward a good destiny; this is remembered as right view
in knowledge, with the quelling of the hope for ‘it exists’ and ‘it does not exist’, there is the surpassing of sin and merit,

children.text: durgateḥ sugateścāsmāt sa mokṣaḥ sabhdirucyate // NRa_1.45 //
children.translated_text: and from bad destiny and good destiny, on that account—this is called <s>mokṣa</s> (liberation)
seeing arising together with its causes, one does not fall into non‑existence,

children.text: astitāmapi nopaiti nirodhaṃ saha hetunā // NRa_1.46 //
children.translated_text: and seeing cessation together with its cause, one does not resort to existence
a cause that is prior‑born or co‑born is, in reality, no cause,
since <s>prajñapti</s> (conceptual designation) is not established, and because, in truth, there is no arising

children.text: asmin satīdaṃ bhavati dīrghe hrasvaṃ yathā sati /
children.translated_text: when this exists, that comes to be—just as, when the long exists, there is the short;
and from the arising of that, this arises—just as light from the arising of a lamp
when the short does not exist, the long does not obtain by its own nature,
and if a lamp is not produced, then the appearance of light is also impossible
thus, seeing the arising of cause and fruit, one does not adopt nihilism,
having admitted, as it is, that this world is born of <s>prapañca</s> (conceptual proliferation)
and, having approached, as it is, the cessation that arises from <s>prapañca</s>,
one does not adopt eternalism; therefore, being resolved on the nondual, one is freed
a form seen from afar is clearly seen when near; if a mirage were water,

children.text: marīciryadi vāri syādāsannaiḥ kiṃ na dṛśyate // NRa_1.52 //
children.translated_text: why is it not seen as such by those who draw near
likewise, this world is seen as it really is by those who have become ‘distant’ (disengaged),
but not thus by those who are ‘near’ (attached), it being <s>animitta</s> (signless), like a mirage
as a mirage, though resembling water, is not water in fact,
so the <s>skandhas</s>, though resembling an <s>ātman</s> (self), are not selves, nor are they real in fact
Vaidya 300
thinking, “this mirage is water,” having conceived thus, one comes here,

children.text: yadi nāstīti tattoyaṃ [gṛṇhīyānmūḍha eva saḥ // NRa_1.55 //
children.translated_text: If he were to say, “it does not exist,” and yet would grasp that water—he is indeed a fool
of one who asserts “it exists thus” regarding the world, which is like a mirage,

children.text: nāstīti cāpi moho 'yaṃ sati mohe na mucyate // NRa_1.56 //
children.translated_text: and of one who says “it does not exist” as well—this is delusion; with delusion present, one is not freed

children.text: nāstiko durgatiṃ yātiṃ sugatiṃ yati cāstikaḥ /
children.translated_text: the <s>nāstika</s> (nihilist) goes to a bad destiny, and the <s>āstika</s> (affirmationist) goes to a good destiny,
but through knowledge of things as they are one attains <s>mokṣa</s> (liberation), resting in the <s>advaya</s> (nondual)
not desiring either <s>nāstitā</s> (non-existence) or <s>astitā</s> (existence), by knowledge as it is,

children.text: nāstitāṃ labhate mohāt kasmānna labhate 'stitām // NRa_1.58 //
children.translated_text: one obtains “non-existence” through delusion—why should one not obtain “existence”
perhaps, from refuting existence, his non-existence is asserted, in reality;
then why, from refuting non-existence, is existence not likewise asserted

children.text: na pratijñā na caritaṃ na cittaṃ bodhiniśrayāt /
children.translated_text: there is no thesis, no practice, no mind, owing to reliance on <s>bodhi</s> (awakening);

children.text: nāstikatve 'rthato yeṣāṃ kathaṃ te nāstikāḥ smṛtāḥ // NRa_1.60 //
children.translated_text: for those, in whose case there is, in reality, no [commitment to] nihilism, how are they remembered as <s>nāstika</s> (nihilists)
ask the world of the <s>Sāṃkhya</s>, <s>Ulūka</s> (Vaiśeṣika), <s>Nirgrantha</s> (Jain), <s>Pudgala</s> (Personalist), and <s>Skandhavādin</s> (Aggregatist),
whether it says there is a transgression beyond “it exists” and “it does not exist”
for this reason, ours is “<s>dharmayautaka</s>” (yoked to the <s>dharmas</s>), there is no transgression of existence and non-existence;
know the nectar of the <s>Buddhas</s>’ teaching to be profound

children.text: vibhavaṃ naiti nāyāti na tiṣṭhatyapi ca kṣaṇam /
children.translated_text: it does not go to disintegration, it does not come, nor does it even abide for a moment,
the world, whose nature is beyond the three times—how could it, in reality
for both, coming and going and standing do not exist in truth,
therefore, what real distinction is there between the world and <s>niryāṇa</s> (going‑out, nirvāṇa)
because there is no standing, arising and cessation are not, in truth,
how, in reality, could there be “arisen,” “standing,” and “ceased”
how could a phenomenon be non‑momentary, if transformation is constant
and if there were no transformation, whence, in reality, would there be otherwiseness

children.text: ekadeśe kṣayādvā syāt kṣaṇikaṃ sarvaśo 'pi vā /
children.translated_text: either from destruction in one part there would be momentariness, or else entirely,
but, since no disparity is perceived, both alternatives are unreasonable
if a phenomenon is wholly momentary, whence any antiquity,
and even if it is non‑momentary due to steadiness, whence any antiquity
as the end of a moment exists, so let its beginning and middle be posited,

children.text: tryātmakatvāt kṣaṇasyaivaṃ na lokasya kṣaṇaṃ sthitiḥ // NRa_1.69 //
children.translated_text: since a moment has a threefold character in this way, the world’s “moment” is not a standing
Vaidya 301
beginnings, middles, and ends are to be considered again, like those of a moment,

children.text: ādimadhyā] vasānatvaṃ na svataḥ parato 'pi vā // NRa_1.70 //
children.translated_text: but the state of having beginning, middle, and end is not from itself nor from another either
it is not one, because it has many parts; nor is there anything partless,
and without the one there is not the many; likewise, non‑existence [depends upon] existence
the non‑existence of existence would be [established] from destruction or from its opposite,

children.text: vināśaḥ pratipakṣo vā kathaṃ syādastyasaṃbhavāt // NRa_1.72 //
children.translated_text: but how could there be destruction or an opposite, if “existence” is impossible
therefore, by <s>nirvṛti</s> (quiescence), the world does not, in reality, incur any diminishment,
and when the question was asked, “is the world finite,” the <s>Jina</s> fell silent
by that very [silence], he is understood by the wise to be a <s>sarvajña</s> (omniscient one),
because this profundity of the <s>Dharma</s> is not to be approached by speech in common usage
thus the <s>Dharma</s> of the highest good (<s>naiḥśreyasa</s>) is profound, without grasping,
it is called <s>anālaya</s> (non‑adherence) by the <s>Saṃbuddhas</s>, the seers of reality
because of this <s>anālaya</s> <s>Dharma</s>, people who delight in <s>ālaya</s> (adherence, clinging),
transgressing “it exists/it does not exist,” being afraid, perish in their lack of wisdom
ruined, they ruin others as well, being fearful of the place of fearlessness,

children.text: tathā kuru yathā rājān naṣṭairna vipraṇāśyase // NRa_1.77 //
children.translated_text: do thus, O king, so that you are not undone by the ruined
just as, when a plantain is split, together with all its parts,
there is nothing, so too a “person,” when split up together with the <s>dhātus</s> (constituents), is nothing
“all <s>dharmas</s> are without self”—therefore this was taught by the <s>Jinas</s>,

children.text: dhātuṣaṭkaṃ ca taiḥ sarvaṃ nirṇitaṃ tacca nārthataḥ // NRa_2.2 //
children.translated_text: and the sixfold <s>dhātu</s> has been entirely determined by them—and that too is not, in reality
neither a self nor a non‑self is found in accordance with reality,
the great sage removed from us the views fabricated on account of self and non‑self

children.text: dṛṣṭaśrutādyaṃ muninā na satyaṃ na mṛṣoditam /
children.translated_text: by the sage, what is seen, heard, and so on was taught as neither true nor false,

children.text: pakṣāddhi pratipakṣaḥ syādubhayaṃ tacca nārthataḥ // NRa_2.4 //
children.translated_text: for from a thesis there would be its antithesis—and both are not, in reality
thus, in the ultimate, this world is beyond truth and untruth,

children.text: asmādeva ca tattvena nopaityasti ca nāsti ca // NRa_2.5 //
children.translated_text: and for this very reason, in suchness, it does not fall under “is” nor under “is not”
and since it is thus “not [to be said] in any way,” how would the <s>sarvajña</s> (omniscient one) speak it
“finite,” or else “infinite,” or “both,” or indeed <s>advaya</s> (non‑dual),
innumerable <s>Buddhas</s> have gone; likewise they will go, and there are those of the present,
and, as for beings, their limit is reckoned by tens of crores; on their account a view arising from the <s>trikāla</s> (three times) is posited,
yet no occurrence of the <s>trikāla</s> (three times) is a cause of the world’s increase or of its decline;

children.text: sarvajñena kathaṃ tasya pūrvānto 'vyākṛtaḥ kṛtaḥ // NRa_2.8 //
children.translated_text: how then would the <s>sarvajña</s> (omniscient one) have made its beginning an <s>avyākṛta</s> (undeclared)
Vaidya 302
but this is the very profundity of the <s>Dharma</s>—and that is hidden from the <s>pṛthagjana</s> (ordinary person),
the world’s being like an illusion is the nectar of the <s>Buddhas</s>’ teaching,

children.text: māyāgajasya dṛśyeta yathā janmānta eva ca /
children.translated_text: as, with a magic‑elephant, one may see it, and likewise an “end of birth,”

children.text: na ca kaścitsa tattvena janmāntaścaiva vidyate // NRa_2.10 //
children.translated_text: yet in reality there is no such thing, nor indeed is there any end of birth;

children.text: māyopamasya lokasya tathā janmānta eva ca /
children.translated_text: so too, for the world, which is like an illusion—and likewise as to an “end of birth,”

children.text: dṛśyate paramārthena na ca janmānta eva ca // NRa_2.11 //
children.translated_text: it is discerned in terms of <s>paramārtha</s> (ultimate truth), and yet there is not, in fact, any end of birth;

children.text: yathā māyāgajo naiti kutaścidyāti na kvacit /
children.translated_text: just as a magic‑elephant neither comes from anywhere nor goes anywhere,
being merely a bewilderment of mind, it does not stand as a real existent,

children.text: tathā māyopamo loko naiti yāti na kutracit /
children.translated_text: so too the world, like an illusion, neither comes nor goes anywhere,
being merely a bewilderment of mind, it does not stand as a real existent,
since thus the world’s very nature is beyond the three times, then, in reality, what could it be,
that it “is,” or “is not,” or would be both, except within <s>vyavahāra</s> (conventional usage)
therefore, the fourfold [question]—finite, infinite, both, and <s>advaya</s> (non‑dual),
was made <s>avyākṛta</s> (undeclared) by the <s>Buddha</s> for this reason, and not for any other,
the impurity of the body is, to be sure, gross and an object of direct perception,

children.text: satataṃ dṛśyamānāpi yadā citta na tiṣṭhati // NRa_2.16 //
children.translated_text: even though constantly seen, when the mind does not abide;
then how will this exceedingly subtle, profound, true <s>Dharma</s> of <s>anālaya</s> (non‑adherence),
being not directly perceptible, readily enter the mind
understanding this, the Sage refrained from teaching the <s>Dharma</s> to us,
having known that, because of its extreme profundity, this <s>Dharma</s> is hard for people to understand;
when misunderstood, this <s>Dharma</s> destroys the unwise,
for, stained by a <s>nāstikī dṛṣṭi</s> (nihilistic view), he sinks into it,
and another, too, through misapprehension of this— a fool fancying himself learned—
his very self ruined by rejection, goes head‑first to <s>Avīci</s>,
just as, with food poorly taken, one comes to ruin,
but, when well taken, one enjoys long life, health, strength, and happiness;
so too, when this is wrongly understood, one comes to ruin,
but, being rightly understood here, one enjoys happiness and attains unsurpassed <s>bodhi</s> (awakening),

children.text: tasmādatra pratikṣepaṃ dṛṣṭiṃ tyaktvā ca nāstikīm /
children.translated_text: therefore here, abandoning rejection and the <s>nāstikī dṛṣṭi</s> (nihilistic view),
make your effort intent on right knowledge for the accomplishment of all aims,
from not fully understanding this <s>Dharma</s>, the conceit “I” persists,

children.text: tataḥ śubhāśubhaṃ karma tato janma śubhāśubham // NRa_2.24 //
children.translated_text: thence [arises] <s>karma</s> (action), wholesome and unwholesome; thence a birth, wholesome and unwholesome,
Vaidya 303
therefore, until the <s>Dharma</s> that cuts off ego‑conceit is understood,
be devoted to the practices of <s>dāna</s> (giving), <s>śīla</s> (morality), and <s>kṣamā</s> (forbearance),
let your undertakings be preceded by <s>Dharma</s> and centered in <s>Dharma</s>, O king,

children.text: sādhayan dharmaniṣṭhāni neha nāmutra sīdati // NRa_2.26 //
children.translated_text: accomplishing what is grounded in <s>Dharma</s>, one does not founder here nor hereafter,

children.text: dharmātkīrtiḥ sukhaṃ caiva neha bhīrna mumūrṣataḥ /
children.translated_text: from <s>Dharma</s> come fame and happiness, and here there is no fear, not even for one at the point of death,

children.text: paralokasukhaṃ sphītaṃ tasmāddharma sadā bhaja // NRa_2.27 //
children.translated_text: and abundant happiness in the other world; therefore always honor <s>Dharma</s>,
<s>Dharma</s> alone is the highest policy; by <s>Dharma</s> the people are won over,

children.text: rañjitena hi lokena neha nāmutra vañcyate // NRa_2.28 //
children.translated_text: and, when the people are won over, one is not defrauded here or hereafter,
but the policy that is by non‑<s>Dharma</s> leaves the people unwon,
and, because the people are not won over, one does not rejoice here or hereafter,
the course that leads to bad destinies is hard for those intent on <s>parātisaṃdhāna</s> (hoarding for others),
what the ill‑wise call “the science of wealth” is a science of misfortune—how have they made it a science of wealth
how is a “man of policy,” intent on <s>parātisaṃdhāna</s> (hoarding for others), truly a man of policy,
by whom, for many thousands of births, his very self is cheated
seeking what is unpleasant for an enemy, abandon faults and rely on virtues,
thus you secure your own welfare, and the enemy’s unpleasant [lot] comes about as well,
by generosity, by pleasant speech, by helpfulness, and by conduct aimed at a single purpose,

children.text: ebhirācara lokasya dharmasyaiva ca saṃgraham // NRa_2.33 //
children.translated_text: with these, effect the winning‑over of the people and, indeed, the winning‑over of <s>Dharma</s>,

children.text: viśvāsaṃ janayatyekaṃ satyaṃ rājñāṃ yathā dṛḍham /
children.translated_text: one thing generates firm trust—<s>satya</s> (truth)—as with kings
Likewise, even what is unreal on their part brings about the utmost distrust,
truth is not [merely] what is “non‑deceptive”; truth, as to its purport, is that which has arisen from reality,
truth is what is exclusively for the other’s benefit, whereas, because it is unbeneficial, what is other than that is false,
one thing—resplendent <s>tyāga</s> (generosity) in kings—covers faults,
and likewise, their <s>kārpaṇya</s> (miserliness) is the destroyer of the entirety of their virtues,
an intellect not to be led away, through being wise—independent of others’ authority and firm—
such a king is not easily deceived; therefore be devoted to <s>prajñā</s> (wisdom),
a king endowed with <s>satya</s> (truth), <s>tyāga</s> (generosity), <s>śama</s> (calm), and <s>prajñā</s> (wisdom)—the four auspicious qualities—
is praised by gods and men as <s>Dharma</s> possessing the four auspicious qualities is praised,
from calmness arises depth, and from depth the highest dignity,
from dignity, radiance of authority; therefore cultivate <s>upaśama</s> (pacification),
for one who constantly sits in the company of restrained speakers, pure, spotless in <s>prajñā</s> (wisdom) and <s>karuṇā</s> (compassion),

children.text: sahāsīnasya satataṃ prajñā dharmaśca vardhate // NRa_2.40 //
children.translated_text: <s>prajñā</s> and <s>Dharma</s> continually increase,
Vaidya 304
those who speak what is salutary are rare; listeners are rarer still,
rarer than they are those who quickly put the salutary into practice,
therefore, knowing what is salutary even if unpleasant, act swiftly,
as a self‑possessed man would drink even a harsh medicine for the sake of health,
ever reflect on the <s>anityatā</s> (impermanence) of life, health, and kingship,
then, stirred by <s>saṃvega</s> (urgency), you will go single‑mindedly toward <s>Dharma</s>,

children.text: avaśyaṃ maraṇaṃ paśyan pāpadduḥkhaṃ mṛtasya ca /
children.translated_text: seeing that death is certain, and the suffering from sin and of the dead,

children.text: ehikena sukhenāpi na pāpaṃ kṣātumarhasi // NRa_2.44 //
children.translated_text: you ought not to do sin, not even for the sake of present worldly pleasure,
if safety is seen somewhere, in a moment fear is seen elsewhere; if there is reassurance in one case,

children.text: yadyekasmin samāśvāsaḥ kimekasminna te bhayam // NRa_2.45 //
children.translated_text: why should there not, for you, be fear in that very one,
from liquor come disgrace in the world, loss of duty, loss of wealth,

children.text: ākāryakaraṇaṃ mohāt[madyaṃ tyaja tataḥ sadā] // NRa_2.46 //
children.translated_text: and, through delusion, doing what should not be done; therefore always abandon liquor,
what is non‑<s>Dharma</s> is, for the most part, praised by those who live upon the king—even when it ought not to be followed—

children.text: ācaran stūyate tasmāt kṛcchrādvetti kṣamākṣamam // NRa_4.1 //
children.translated_text: therefore he learns only with difficulty what is pardonable and unpardonable; if even some other person can endure harsh, unpleasant speech,
how much more should you, O king, great lord of the earth,

children.text: kimu rājā mahābhaumastvaṃ mayā bhikṣuṇā satā // NRa_4.2 //
children.translated_text: from me, a virtuous <s>bhikṣu</s> (monk),
indeed, out of affection for you and out of compassion for the world on your account,

children.text: ahameko vadāmi tvāṃ pathyamapyapriyaṃ bhṛśam // NRa_4.3 //
children.translated_text: I alone speak to you what is salutary even though very unpleasant,
“at the right time, with compassion, one should address the disciple with what is true, smooth, meaningful, and salutary,” said the <s>Bhagavān</s> (Blessed One),
therefore you are being addressed just so,

children.text: akrodhe satyavākye ca ślādhyamāno yadi sthitaḥ /
children.translated_text: if, remaining free from anger and in truthful speech, when being praised he stands firm,
he should receive what is to be heard, like water fit to be poured upon one being bathed,

children.text: tasya me vadato vākyaṃ tvamihāmutra ca kṣamam /
children.translated_text: therefore, as I speak, may you be forbearing toward my words here and hereafter,

children.text: jñātvā kuru hitāyedamātmano jagato 'pi ca // NRa_4.6 //
children.translated_text: having understood, do this for the welfare of yourself and of the world as well,
if, having obtained wealth, you will not give to petitioners before they depart,
then, through ingratitude and greed, you will not obtain wealth again,

children.text: iha pathyadanaṃ loke na vahatyabhṛto bhṛtaḥ /
children.translated_text: here in the world, a hired carrier does not carry when unpaid,
but a beggar, though unpaid, yonder bears one a hundredfold,
be ever of a generous mind, delighting in generous deeds,
for one whose actions are generous, all the fruit that arises is generous,
Vaidya 305
establish a splendid abode of <s>Dharma</s>, renowned, a seat of the <s>Ratnatraya</s> (Three Jewels),
one not sullied by the feeble daydreams of [other] kings,
a <s>Dharma</s>-foundation that does not make neighboring kings’ hairs stand on end—
better not to have built that, O king, for it brings disrepute even after death,
by the utmost generosity, cause an increase of amazement and zeal among the generous,

children.text: utsāhanghaṃ ca mandānāṃ sarvasvenāpi kāraya // NRa_4.12 //
children.translated_text: and bring about zeal even among the sluggish, doing so even with all your wealth,
your entire wealth must, perforce, be left and go elsewhere,

children.text: dharme niyuktaṃ yātyeva purastātsarvameva tat // NRa_4.13 //
children.translated_text: yet what is assigned to <s>Dharma</s> surely goes on ahead, all of it,
all the wealth of the former king has come under the sway of the [present] king,

children.text: kiṃ pūrvakasya dharmāya sukhāya yaśase 'pi vā // NRa_4.14 //
children.translated_text: what, of the former, remained for <s>Dharma</s>, or for happiness, or even for fame,
from wealth enjoyed, there is happiness here; from wealth given, happiness in the next world,
from wealth neither enjoyed nor given—since it is lost—there is only suffering; whence happiness
when you are perishing, because of lack of independence you will not be able to give, being under ministers,
by ministers devoid of affection, who would cut you off in adversity, seeking the favor of a new king,
therefore, even at the cost of all your wealth, remaining self‑possessed, quickly establish an abode of <s>Dharma</s> (righteousness),
standing amid the certainty of death like a lamp set in a wind;
and the departments charged with <s>Dharma</s> and the other institutions instituted by former kings,
let those too—even the <s>Devadroṇī</s> (religious endowment vessel) and the like—be set going as they stand,
let them be attended by men practicing <s>ahiṃsā</s> (non‑violence), of good conduct, firm in vows, fond of guests,
forbearing toward all, non‑quarrelsome, ever ready,
the blind, the diseased, the maimed, the miserable, the orphaned, and the forest‑folk,
let they too obtain food and drink equally, without obstruction,
set in motion benefactions, even for the unfortunate, of the good and the righteous,
and likewise those appropriate from the institutions of other realms,
in all jurisdictions over <s>Dharma</s>, appoint a <s>dharmādhikṛta</s> (superintendent of Dharma) who is upright—

children.text: alubdhaṃ paṇḍitaṃ dharmyaṃ kuru tesāmabādhakam // NRa_4.22 //
children.translated_text: non‑greedy, learned, righteous—make him not oppressive to them,
appoint as ministers those versed in policy, righteous, affectionate, pure, devoted and unafraid,

children.text: kulīnān śīlasaṃpannān kṛtajñān sacivān kuru // NRa_4.23 //
children.translated_text: of good family, endowed with character, and grateful,
appoint as magistrates men who are not petty, who are liberal, brave, affectionate, sharing enjoyments, steadfast,
ever vigilant, and righteous,
appoint as senior officials those whose character is grounded in <s>Dharma</s>, pure, capable, knowing how to conduct affairs, skilled in the treatises,

children.text: kṛtavṛttīn samān snigdhān vṛddhānadhikṛtān kuru // NRa_4.25 //
children.translated_text: of established conduct, impartial, affectionate, and elders,
Vaidya 306
and every month, from them hear all income and expenditure,

children.text: śrutvā dharmādhikārādyaṃ kāryaṃ sarvaṃ svayaṃ vada // NRa_4.26 //
children.translated_text: having heard, yourself declare all that is to be done, beginning with the Department of <s>Dharma</s>,

children.text: dharmārthaṃ yadi te rājyaṃ na kīrtyarthaṃ na kāmataḥ /
children.translated_text: if your kingship is for the sake of <s>Dharma</s>, not for the sake of fame nor out of desire,
then it is exceedingly fruitful; otherwise, it is for misfortune,
since in this world, O king, people for the most part become bait to one another,

children.text: yathā rājyaṃ ca dharmaśca bhavettava tathā śṛṇu // NRa_4.28 //
children.translated_text: listen, then, how both your kingdom and <s>Dharma</s> may be preserved for you,
let there be gathered for you many who are mature in knowledge, born in good families, knowing justice, fearing sin,

children.text: sametā bahavo nityaṃ santu te kāryadarśinaḥ // NRa_4.29 //
children.translated_text: ever observers of affairs,
even if they, acting according to justice, inflict punishments, imprisonments, beatings, and the like,

children.text: kāruṇyārdraḥ sadā bhūtvā tvamanugrahavān bhava // NRa_4.30 //
children.translated_text: you, always softened by <s>karuṇā</s> (compassion), be gracious,
you should raise your mind solely for the welfare of all embodied beings,
out of <s>kāruṇya</s> (compassion) always, O king, even toward those who commit grave sins,
for toward grievous sinners, the violent, mercy is to be shown especially,

children.text: ta eva hi kṛpāsthānaṃ hatātmāno mahātmanām // NRa_4.32 //
children.translated_text: they indeed, ruined in themselves, are the proper object of mercy for the great‑souled,

children.text: pratyahaṃ pañcarātraṃ vā baddhān kṣīṇān vimocaya /
children.translated_text: every day, or every five nights, release those bound whose [term] is spent,

children.text: śeṣānapi yathāyogaṃ mā kāṃścit naiva mocaya // NRa_4.33 //
children.translated_text: and others too according to what is fitting; but release none who should not be released,
for in those in whom a mind of non‑release arises, there arises non‑restraint,
therefore, from non‑restraint, sin continually accumulates,
so long as they are not released, let them be bound comfortably,
provided with barbering, bathing, drink, food, medicine, and clothing,
as in the case of unworthy sons, from a wish to make them worthy,
correction is to be done out of <s>kāruṇya</s> (compassion), not from hatred, not from desire of gain,
having reflected and ascertained rightly, even in the case of the depraved, the murderous,

children.text: ahatvā pīḍayitvā ca kuru nirviṣayān narān // NRa_4.37 //
children.translated_text: without killing, after punishing, make men deprived of their domain (resources),

children.text: svatantraḥ paśya sarvaṃ ca viṣayaṃ cāracakṣuṣā /
children.translated_text: being independent, survey all your realm with the eye of spies,

children.text: nityāpramattaḥ smṛtimān kuru kāryaṃ ca dhārmikam // NRa_4.38 //
children.translated_text: ever unremiss and mindful, do also what accords with <s>Dharma</s>,
by gifts, honor, and respectful treatment, ever cherish the seats of merit (the worthy),
and the rest also, with generous and appropriate measures, according to rule,
the royal tree—its blossoms made luxuriant by honor, its great fruit gift,
its shade forbearance—is frequented by the birds that are its servants,
a king composed of the quality of <s>tyāga</s> (generosity) becomes brilliant and beloved,
like a sugar‑sweet, even though rough with cardamom and pepper,
Vaidya 307
thus your rule will not be by <s>mātsyanyāya</s> (the law of the fish), but by justice,

children.text: na cānyāyo na vādharmo dharmaścaivaṃ bhaviṣyati // NRa_4.42 //
children.translated_text: neither injustice nor non‑<s>Dharma</s> will there be; thus there will be <s>Dharma</s>,
you did not bring kingship from the other world, nor will you carry it there,
it was obtained through <s>Dharma</s>; therefore, for its sake you ought not to commit non‑<s>Dharma</s>,
with kingship, with the price of goods, [there comes] a succession of the wares of suffering,

children.text: rājan yathā nārjayasi prayatnaḥ kriyatāṃ tathā // NRa_4.44 //
children.translated_text: O king, let effort be made in such a way that you do not amass [for yourself],
from the succession of royal stores that arises from kingship and the price of goods,

children.text: rājan yathā nirviśasi prayatnaḥ kriyatāṃ tathā // NRa_4.45 //
children.translated_text: O king, let effort be made in such a way that you extricate yourself from it
Even on obtaining the earth with its four continents as a <s>cakravartin</s> (wheel‑turning emperor),

children.text: śārīraṃ mānasaṃ caiva sukhadvayamidaṃ matam // NRa_4.46 //
children.translated_text: this twofold <s>sukha</s> (pleasure), bodily and mental, is what is held [to exist]
Bodily <s>vedanā</s> (feeling)‑pleasure is merely a counter‑measure to <s>duḥkha</s> (suffering),

children.text: saṃjñāmayaṃ mānasaṃ tu kevalaṃ kalpanākṛtam // NRa_4.47 //
children.translated_text: whereas the mental is fashioned solely by <s>saṃjñā</s> (conception), as mere imagination
merely a counter‑measure to <s>duḥkha</s>, and merely a construct of fancy,
this—what the world takes to be the whole of <s>sukha</s>—is, in truth, futile
As for regions, districts, cities, dwellings, areas and places of residence,
beds, food and drink, elephants, horses, and women—each is enjoyed only one at a time

children.text: yadā ca yatra cittaṃ syāt tadānena sukhaṃ kila /
children.translated_text: And whenever and wherever the mind is, then by that there is pleasure,
through non‑attention to the rest, the others are, in truth, futile
If the five <s>indriyas</s> (sense faculties)—eye and the rest—while grasping the five <s>viṣayas</s> (objects),

children.text: na kalpayati cedgaṇhan nāsmātteṣu tadā sukham // NRa_4.51 //
children.translated_text: do not project constructions, then there is no <s>sukha</s> for us in them

children.text: jānīte viṣayaṃ yaṃ yaṃ yena yenendriyeṇa ca /
children.translated_text: Whatever object is known, and by whatever <s>indriya</s>,

children.text: tadā na śeṣaiḥ śeṣāṇi vyarthānyeva yatastadā // NRa_4.52 //
children.translated_text: at that time the remaining [faculties] regarding the remaining [objects] are simply futile
The mind, having apprehended the form of an object obtained by the senses,

children.text: upalabhya vyatītasya kalpayan manyate sukham // NRa_4.53 //
children.translated_text: apprehending its shape and constructing what is past, imagines <s>sukha</s>
Although here a single <s>indriya</s> knows a single object,

children.text: tadapyarthaṃ vinā vyarthaṃ vyartho 'rtho 'pi ca tadvinā // NRa_4.54 //
children.translated_text: even that is useless without the object, and the object likewise is useless without that
Just as, depending (<s>pratītya</s>) on mother and father, the coming‑into‑being of a son is said,
so, depending on eye and form, is said the arising of <s>vijñāna</s> (cognition)
Past and future objects, together with the <s>indriyas</s>, are futile,

children.text: tadudvayānatiriktatvād vyarthā ye 'pi ca sāṃpratāḥ // NRa_4.56 //
children.translated_text: and those that are present are futile as well, since they are not apart from that dyad
Just as the eye, through error, apprehends a circle of a firebrand,
so the <s>indriyas</s> apprehend the objects as if they were presently existing
Vaidya 308
The <s>indriyas</s> and the objects of the <s>indriyas</s> are considered to be composed of the <s>pañcabhūta</s> (five elements),
because, taken individually, each element is useless, these [faculties and objects] are, in truth, futile
A fire without fuel results when the elements are taken in separated portions,
while in their contact the individual marks are absent; this determination applies to the rest as well
Thus, whether in separation or in conjunction, because of the futility of the elements, their coming‑together is vain,
and because of the futility of that conjunction, <s>rūpa</s> (form/matter) is, in truth, futile
For <s>vijñāna</s> (cognition), <s>vedanā</s> (feeling), <s>saṃjñā</s> (perception), and <s>saṃskāra</s> (formations), in every respect,
there is, in <s>paramārtha</s> (ultimate truth), a twofold futility, due to the futility of each taken in itself
The conceit of <s>sukha</s> with respect to <s>duḥkha</s> occurs, in reality, only at its counter‑action,
and likewise the conceit of <s>sukha</s> concerning <s>sukha</s> itself is born from opposition [to it]
Thus, the craving (<s>tṛṣṇā</s>) for union (<s>saṃyoga</s>) with <s>sukha</s> is abandoned, due to its lack of own‑being (<s>svabhāva</s>),

children.text: duḥkhe viyogatṛṣṇā ca paśyatāṃ muktirityataḥ // NRa_4.63 //
children.translated_text: and the craving for disunion (<s>viyoga</s>) from <s>duḥkha</s>; therefore, for those who see, that is liberation
If it be asked, “Who sees?”, ‘<s>citta</s> (mind)’ is spoken by way of <s>vyavahāra</s> (convention),

children.text: na hi caittaṃ vinā cittaṃ vyarthatvānna saheṣyate // NRa_4.64 //
children.translated_text: for without the <s>caittas</s> (mental factors) there is no tolerable <s>citta</s>, owing to its futility
Thus, having known the world to be futile, as it really is, being without a support,
one becomes extinguished, without appropriation (<s>upādāna</s>), like a fire without fuel (<s>nirupādāna</s>‑fire)
Even a <s>Bodhisattva</s>, seeing thus, is considered fixed in <s>saṃbodhi</s> (full awakening),
only through his <s>kāruṇyā</s> (compassion) does the continuum of becoming persist until awakening
The <s>saṃbhāra</s> (accumulation/equipment) of the <s>Bodhisattva</s> in the <s>Mahāyāna</s> (Great Vehicle) has been set forth by the <s>Tathāgata</s>s,

children.text: nirdiṣṭaḥ sa tu saṃmūḍhaiḥ pradviṣṭaścaiva nindyate // NRa_4.67 //
children.translated_text: but that is hated and reviled by the thoroughly deluded
Whether one unacquainted with merits and faults, or one who takes faults to be present in merits,
or else a hater of merits—he is a reviler of the <s>Mahāyāna</s>
Knowing the faults of those who harm others, and the merits of those who benefit others,
one who hates merits is called a reviler of the <s>Mahāyāna</s>
Because the <s>Mahāyāna</s>, a mine of merits, is dear for being solely of the flavor of others’ welfare and for disregarding self‑interest,

children.text: guṇākaraṃ mahāyānaṃ taddviṣī tena dahyate // NRa_4.70 //
children.translated_text: whoever hates that is burned by that very thing
Even a man of <s>śraddha</s> (faith), by a wrong grasping, may come to hate, or the other, being angry,

children.text: śrāddho 'pi dagdha ityuktaḥ kā cintā dveṣābandhure // NRa_4.71 //
children.translated_text: even a faithful one is said to be ‘burned’; what need to consider one bound to hatred
Even by poison can poison be destroyed, as is stated by physicians,
If it is said, “Even by <s>duḥkha</s> (suffering) one should destroy what is unbeneficial,” what is thereby opposed
on the basis of the scriptural statement, “the <s>dharmas</s> (phenomena) are mind‑preceded; mind is foremost,”

children.text: hitaṃ hitamanāḥ kurvan duḥkhenāpyahitaṃ katham // NRa_4.73 //
children.translated_text: how could one whose mind is on the beneficial, doing the beneficial, produce the unbeneficial even by <s>duḥkha</s>
Vaidya 309
Even <s>duḥkha</s> that is wholesome for the future should be undertaken; how much more [so] beneficial <s>sukha</s>,

children.text: ātmanaśca pareṣāṃ ca dharma eṣā sanātanaḥ // NRa_4.74 //
children.translated_text: this is the perennial <s>dharma</s> (norm) for oneself and for others
If, by abandoning sense‑pleasure, afterward there is abundant <s>sukha</s>,

children.text: tyajenmātrāsukhaṃ dhīraḥ saṃpaśyan vipulaṃ sukham // NRa_4.75 //
children.translated_text: seeing the abundant <s>sukha</s>, the steadfast should relinquish sense‑pleasure
And if this were not accepted by one who dispenses bitter medicine,

children.text: tataścikitsakādyāśca hatā naivaṃ ca yujyate // NRa_4.76 //
children.translated_text: then physicians and the like would be refuted; but that is not reasonable
What is sometimes seen as unwholesome is, at times, judged wholesome by the learned,
for general rule and exception are praised in all treatises
All the emanations, preceded by <s>karuṇā</s> (compassion) and made pure by knowledge,
are declared in the <s>Mahāyāna</s>—who, being sentient, would revile that
Because of its extreme generosity and profoundness, by despondent, untrained persons,
the <s>Mahāyāna</s> is reviled today, out of delusion, by those hostile to themselves and to others

Since the <s>Mahāyāna</s> has the nature of <s>dāna</s> (giving), <s>śīla</s> (morality), <s>kṣamā</s> (forbearance), <s>vīrya</s> (energy), <s>dhyāna</s> (meditative absorption), <s>prajñā</s> (wisdom), and <s>kṛpā</s> (compassion),
why speak ill against it
Others’ welfare is through <s>dāna</s> and <s>śīla</s>, and one’s own through <s>kṣānti</s> (forbearance) and <s>vīrya</s>,

children.text: dhyānaṃ prajñā ca mokṣāya mahāyānārthasaṃgrahaḥ // NRa_4.81 //
children.translated_text: <s>dhyāna</s> and <s>prajñā</s> are for liberation—this is the compendium of the aims of the <s>Mahāyāna</s>
For the sake of others’ welfare, one’s own welfare, and liberation—such, in brief, is the <s>Buddha</s>’s dispensation,
these being wombed in the six <s>pāramitā</s>s (perfections); therefore this utterance is Buddhist
